content: Gemfibrozil is a medication prescribed to help reduce cholesterol and certain fatty substances in the blood. It is used in conjunction with dietary changes, such as limiting cholesterol and fat intake. The accumulation of cholesterol and fats along the walls of arteries, a condition known as atherosclerosis, can reduce blood flow and oxygen supply to the heart, brain, and other parts of the body. By lowering blood levels of cholesterol and fats, gemfibrozil may help prevent heart disease, chest pain (angina), strokes, and heart attacks. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Gemfibrozil is available in tablet and capsule form and is taken orally. It is typically taken twice daily, 30 minutes before the morning and evening meals. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take gemfibrozil exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Continue taking gemfibrozil even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking gemfibrozil, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to gemfibrozil or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (blood thinners) like warfarin (Coumadin) and vitamins. If you are taking insulin or oral diabetes medications, your dose may need to be adjusted because gemfibrozil can increase blood sugar levels. Discuss any dose changes with your doctor. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have or have ever had ulcers, diabetes, or gallbladder, kidney, or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, let your doctor know. If you become pregnant while taking gemfibrozil, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform the doctor or dentist that you are taking gemfibrozil. While taking gemfibrozil, adhere to a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet. This diet should include foods like cottage cheese, fat-free milk, fish (not canned in oil), vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils and margarines (such as corn, safflower, canola, and soybean oils). Avoid foods high in fat, such as meat (especially liver and fatty cuts), egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, shortening, lard, pastries, cakes, cookies, gravy, peanut butter, chocolate, olives, potato chips, coconut, cheese (other than cottage cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, and fried foods. If you miss a dose of gemfibrozil, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Gemfibrozil may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: stomach pain, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, gas, headache, dizziness, blurred vision, or flushing. If you experience muscle pain or weakness, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store gemfibrozil in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to gemfibrozil. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
